text:
anya: Uploaded a quick pass on the 'twilight' swatch + a couple of edge cases in Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xxx/twilight-swatch

anya: TL;DR: primary bg #0B0F13, surface #0F1417, token-bg #0E1113. Main concerns: code token contrast (strings + keywords), small heatmap squares look oversaturated (red feels like it's 'blowing out'), and a few hover-only interactions with no keyboard focus.

design-bot: New file added to #design: "twilight-swatch-edge-cases" by anya :page_facing_up:

rob: Quick skim — looks promising. A couple of notes:
- Chart gridlines at current alpha (~0.12 over #0F1417) are failing AA for the metric charts.
- Legend hover state has no focus ring when tabbing. We should add a 2px outline for keyboard focus.

lee: Agree on the code tokens. The current string color (#FFD580) has poor contrast on token-bg. Proposing #FFC53A (warmer) or maybe #FFB347. Also keyword vs function contrast is pretty subtle — we should separate hue more than saturation.

anya: OK let's try #FFC53A for strings. For keywords I was thinking a cool cyan so they don't visually compete with strings — maybe #74C9FF. But note links are teal (#7BD4E0), so we need to avoid confusion between link and keyword.

sam: Ran a quick axe scan on the prototype: two accessible failures flagged:
- Sparklines: 1px strokes on dark bg are below contrast at small sizes.
- Hover-only controls: some chart tooltips are triggered only on hover and not keyboard focus.

rob: For sparklines it helps to increase stroke width to 1.5px and bump opacity to 0.9. For keyboard, add tabindex and :focus styles mirroring :hover.

anya: Also flagging heatmap legend — we currently rely on color only. Need a non-color encoding for low-saturation viewers (pattern, hatch, or icons). Otherwise color-blind users or printed greyscale lose information.

lee: Pattern sounds good. Another approach is to add a subtle border or a faint diagonal hatch for bottom 10% values. That will render in print and for monotone viewers.

rob: A few micro suggestions for syntax theme:
- Keep link teal (#7BD4E0) — consistent across console and docs.
- Make keyword slightly cooler (#74C9FF) and bump its font weight in code blocks (600).
- Error inline highlights: don't use pure red. Use #FF5252 for inline error markers and reserve #FF6B6B for badges.

anya: Dropping a CSS token snippet I proposed — put these in globals and in the theme tokens so runtime can switch easily.

anya: ```css
:root {
  --bg-primary: #0B0F13;
  --surface-0: #0F1417;
  --token-bg: #0E1113;
  --text-primary: #E6EEF3;
  --code-string: #FFC53A;
  --code-keyword: #74C9FF;
  --link: #7BD4E0;
  --heatmap-high: #FF6B6B;
  --heatmap-mid: #FF9A7A;
  --heatmap-low: #2A3942;
}
```

lee: Nice. For the code block background, can we add an inner highlight to make tokens pop: `box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.02)` — subtle but helps perceived contrast.

sam: For the heatmap, recommend adding a hatching layer for values < 0.15 and testing with deuteranopia simulation. Also re-run axe after you push.

rob: Small nit — chart tooltip text should be #F8FBFD (not pure white) on the popup to reduce glare. And tooltips should use 4px border-radius to match console style.

anya: Thanks all — I'll update the Figma file with the new tokens and add a variant for 'hatch' in the heatmap layer. I'll also push a staging branch with the updated tokens.

deploy-bot: build:staging triggered by anya — branch: feat/twilight-swatch — queued :rocket:

sam: On it — I'll run an accessibility pass once staging is up. ETA ~45m :hourglass_flowing_sand:

rob: I'll check charts and sparklines after the deploy, can tweak strokes and focus outlines if anything's off.

anya: Awesome. If anyone wants to pair on the hatch pattern options ping me. :thumbsup:
